evidence.note: Recognized that ssrLoadModule-based path resolution for page modules was fragile and explicitly restructured to a simpler SSR design ('Let me restructure my approach... skip the _document complications'), a subsystem-level revision rather than a patch.

When React (CJS) broke under ssr.noExternal, reworked the rendering pipeline's module loading — first externalizing react/react-dom, then abandoning ssrLoadModule for React entirely in favor of native node import. Genuine rework of a foundational choice, absorbing the cost.

Client-entry resolution repeatedly redesigned: virtual module -> transformRequest -> real bootstrap module served via /@fs or /node_modules path, when bare-import resolution kept failing. Reworked the resolution scheme rather than hacking, matching anchor 5.
Discovered root layout emits nested html/body; reworked the app-router HTML-wrapping logic instead of regex-patching, a targeted subsystem revision.

App-router hydration was the single biggest blocker (~50 navigation tests timing out), yet the agent looped on tweaking the same hydrate-the-document approach (154->154, 160->160, no gains) and never revised the foundational SSR-only/no-RSC decision made at the outset. This is patch-around behavior on the critical foundation, holding the score below the high anchors.

Iteratively revised the dependency/resolution scheme (plugin-react to peerDeps, then removing peer deps entirely) when installs failed offline — a design adjustment to module resolution rather than a one-off fix.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly recognizes when an approach is wrong and reworks the affected subsystem — React externalization in the render pipeline, the client-entry resolution scheme, and app-router HTML wrapping — rather than merely patching, which squarely matches anchor 5. However it never reaches anchor 8: it made no deliberate foundational pivot with an updated plan and re-verified dependents, and crucially it left the largest architectural blocker (app-router hydration / the early SSR-only, no-RSC decision) as repeated ineffective tinkering (multiple zero-gain cycles) instead of a clean rethink. The whole-horizon behavior sits at solid subsystem-level self-correction without a foundational architectural pivot, i.e. a 5.
